mainTopic: When and how the משיח will come: the fixed time versus merit, signs of the קץ, and stories about the גאולה.
overview: The amud opens at the end of the debate between רבי אליעזר, who ties the גאולה to תשובה, and רבי יהושע, who says it has a fixed time. רבי יהושע's proof from the oath in דניאל leaves רבי אליעזר silent. The גמרא then lists signs of the קץ. These include fruit returning to ארץ ישראל, hard times with no wages and no peace, no fish even for a sick person, and the end of the lowly kingdom, the arrogant, and the current judges. עולא and רב פפא add that ירושלים is redeemed through צדקה, and that fixing arrogance and corrupt judges removes the foreign oppressors. רבי יוחנן teaches that a shrinking or troubled generation should expect the משיח, and that he comes to a generation that is all righteous or all guilty. רבי יהושע בן לוי resolves two contradictions with one idea: if ישראל merit, the גאולה comes early and gloriously; if not, it comes in its time and humbly. Stories follow: שמואל answers King שבור, רבי יהושע בן לוי meets אליהו and the משיח, who says he will come 'today, if you listen to His voice', and רבי יוסי בן קיסמא's prediction is confirmed by a sign. The amud ends with his deathbed request to bury his coffin deep, and the reason comes on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רבי יהושע's proof that kings will bow without תשובה
steps.stepSummary: The text opens in the middle of a פסוק from ישעיהו that רבי יהושע was quoting. The פסוק says kings will rise and princes will bow to Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: [As the פסוק says:] 'Kings shall see and arise, princes shall bow down.'
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the argument in the middle. רבי יהושע is finishing a פסוק he quoted to show that the גאולה will come even without תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full פסוק describes Israel as despised and enslaved, yet kings will still bow to them. רבי יהושע reads this to mean the גאולה comes at a set time, even while Israel is still in a low state and has not done תשובה.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the last part of a פסוק רבי יהושע began quoting before this section starts.

phrases.english: Kings shall see and arise,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 49:7. This is the end of a פסוק רבי יהושע started quoting just before this.

phrases.english: princes shall bow down?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְלָכִים יִרְאוּ וָקָמוּ שָׂרִים וְיִשְׁתַּחֲווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יהושע's proof from the part of the argument that comes before this section.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the גאולה does not depend on תשובה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר answers with 'Return, Israel'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר brings a פסוק from ירמיהו in which ה׳ calls on Israel to return. This shows that the גאולה depends on תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: But isn't it already stated, 'If you will return, Israel, says ה׳, return to Me'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר pushes back against רבי יהושע with a פסוק that links the return to ה׳ with Israel's own return.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר reads the פסוק as a condition: if Israel returns, then ה׳ will bring them back. That supports his view that the גאולה is tied to תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it already stated? This is a way of bringing a counter-פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
But isn't it already stated:
"If you will return, Israel,
says the Lord, return to Me"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters רבי יהושע's פסוק with a פסוק that supports the other side.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the גאולה depends on תשובה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע brings the sworn time from דניאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע quotes דניאל, where an angel swears that the end will come at a fixed time: 'a time, times and a half'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: But isn't it already stated, 'I heard the man clothed in linen, above the waters of the river, lift his right and left hand to heaven and swear by the One Who lives forever that it will be for a time, times and a half, and when the crushing of the power of the holy people is finished, all these will end'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers with a פסוק showing that the end has a set date, which was sworn to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath about a fixed time means the date is already set. It does not wait for Israel's תשובה. This is a strong proof for רבי יהושע's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Clothed in linen. This is the angel in דניאל's vision.
For a time, times and a half. This is a fixed period.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
But isn't it already stated:
"And I heard the man clothed in linen,
who was above the waters of the river,
and he lifted his right hand and his left hand to heaven,
and swore by the One Who lives forever
that it shall be for a time, times, and a half;
and when the crushing of the power of the holy people is completed,
all these shall be finished, etc."?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אליעזר's פסוק with a stronger one about a set, sworn date.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the גאולה has a fixed time and does not depend on תשובה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר is silent
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר has no answer, and the argument ends there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The debate ends. רבי אליעזר does not answer רבי יהושע's last proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silence shows that רבי אליעזר could not refute the פסוק from דניאל. In this exchange, רבי יהושע's view has the last word.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר holds that the גאולה depends on תשובה, and רבי יהושע holds that it has a set time. רבי יהושע's proof from the oath in דניאל ends the debate.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer was silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשָׁתַק רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the debate after רבי יהושע's proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהושע's proof stands, and רבי אליעזר does not refute it.

steps.title: רבי אבא: fruit growing on Israel's mountains is the clearest sign
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says the clearest sign of the קץ is when the land of Israel produces fruit in abundance, based on a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבא said: There is no more revealed sign of the end than this, as it says: 'And you, mountains of Israel, you shall give your branches and bear your fruit for My people Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: signs that the משיח is about to come. רבי אבא gives the first sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the land, which had been barren during the exile, starts producing fruit richly again, that shows Israel is about to return. The פסוק goes on to say they will soon be coming.

keyTerms.meaning: The end, meaning the time of the גאולה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abba said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ קֵץ מְגוּלֶּה מִזֶּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר:
phrases.english: You have no more revealed sign of the end than this, as it is stated:
"But you, mountains of Israel,
you shall give your branches and yield your fruit
to My people Israel, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אֵין לְךָ קֵץ מְגוּלֶּה מִזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new statement about the signs of the קץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An abundance of fruit in ארץ ישראל is the clearest sign of the קץ.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: no wages and no peace are also a sign
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר adds another sign from זכריה: when there are no wages for people or animals, and no peace for those going out and coming in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: This is also a sign, as it says: 'For before those days there was no wage for man nor wage for animal, and for the one going out and coming in there was no peace from the oppressor.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives a second sign of the קץ, this time a hard economic and social situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי אבא's good sign, this one is a time of trouble. There is no work, there is no income from renting animals, and there is no safety. The פסוק describes the hard times that come just before the good days.

keyTerms.meaning: Also from this. It adds another sign.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: Also from this,
as it is stated: "For before those days
there was no hire for man,
nor any hire for beast,
and for the one going out and the one coming in
there is no peace from the oppressor."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר אַף מִזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second sign of the קץ to רבי אבא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lack of work wages and a lack of peace are also signs of the קץ.

steps.title: What does 'no peace for the one going out and coming in' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the last phrase in רבי אליעזר's פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'for the one going out and coming in there is no peace from the oppressor'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what this unclear phrase means. This sets up two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is unclear. Who exactly will have no peace, and what does צר mean here? The answers of רב and שמואל will each explain it differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What? The גמרא uses it to ask for an explanation.
For the one going out and the one coming in

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "for the one going out and the one coming in
there is no peace from the oppressor"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לַיּוֹצֵא וְלַבָּא אֵין שָׁלוֹם מִן הַצָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what part of the פסוק רבי אליעזר quoted means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'no peace for the one going out and coming in'.

steps.title: רב: even תלמידי חכמים will have no peace
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that even תלמידי חכמים, who are promised peace, will not have peace because of the oppressor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Even תלמידי חכמים, about whom peace is written, as it says 'Great peace to those who love Your Torah', will have no peace because of the oppressor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first explanation. The trouble will be so great that it reaches even the people promised peace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads 'the one going out and coming in' as including even תלמידי חכמים. Normally the פסוק in תהלים promises them great peace, but before the משיח comes, even they will suffer from the oppressor.

phrases.english: Rav said: Even Torah scholars,
about whom peace is written,
as it is written: "Great peace to those who love Your Torah,"
will have no peace because of the oppressor.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר אַף תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the meaning of the phrase.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even תלמידי חכמים, who are promised peace, will have no peace from the oppressor.

steps.title: שמואל: until all prices are equal
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains the phrase differently: the משיח will come only when all prices are equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: Until all the prices are all equal.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second, different explanation of the phrase, based on market prices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב focused on people and their safety, while שמואל focuses on the market. In his reading, the sign is that all prices will be equal.

keyTerms.meaning: Market prices (not gates, in this context)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two signs of the קץ: abundant fruit (רבי אבא) and hard times with no wages and no peace (רבי אליעזר). רב explains the 'no peace' to include even תלמידי חכמים, while שמואל explains it as all prices being equal.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כׇּל הַשְּׁעָרִים כּוּלָּן שְׁקוּלִין.
phrases.english: Until all the prices are all equal.
phrases.notes: Here שְׁעָרִים means market prices, not gates.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר עַד שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כׇּל הַשְּׁעָרִים כּוּלָּן שְׁקוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question that רב answered.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sign is that all market prices will be equal.

steps.title: No fish to be found even for a sick person
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says בן דוד will not come until a small fish is wanted for a sick person and none can be found. He proves it from two פסוקים in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: בן דוד will not come until people look for a small fish for a sick person and cannot find one. As it says: 'Then I will make their waters sink and make their rivers flow like oil.' And right after that it says: 'On that day I will cause a horn to grow for the house of ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא adds a new sign before the משיח comes: fish will become so rare that even a sick person cannot get one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק describes rivers sinking and flowing slowly like oil, so the fish disappear. The second פסוק, which the גמרא introduces with 'it is written after it', speaks of ישראל's 'horn' growing, meaning redemption. Putting them in this order shows that the shortage comes first and redemption follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The son of דוד, meaning the משיח
And it is written after it: the next פסוק that follows

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said:
The son of David will not come
until a [small] fish is sought for a sick person
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in some versions; others just say 'a fish.'

phrases.english: and it will not be found,
as it is stated: 'Then I will make their waters sink
and make their rivers flow like oil,'
and it is written after it:
'On that day I will cause a horn to grow for the house of Israel.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 29:21. A 'horn' is a picture of strength and glory.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: אֵין בֶּן דָּוִד בָּא עַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another sign to the list of signs before the משיח, following the earlier statements of רבי אבא, רבי אליעזר, רב and שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before the משיח comes, fish will be so scarce that one cannot be found even for a sick person.

steps.title: The lowly kingdom must end its rule over ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא says בן דוד will not come until the 'lowly kingdom' no longer rules over ישראל. He reads a word play into a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר חנינא said: בן דוד will not come until the lowly kingdom ends its rule over ישראל. As it says: 'He will cut off the sprigs with pruning hooks.' And right after that it says: 'At that time a gift will be brought to ה׳ צבאות from a people pulled and plucked.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא בר חנינא gives another sign: the foreign kingdom that rules over ישראל must first come to an end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He hears the word הזלזלים (sprigs) as a hint to מלכות הזלה, the lowly kingdom. Cutting off the sprigs means that kingdom is cut off. Then the following פסוק describes ישראל bringing a gift to ה׳, which is the redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: The lowly or cheap kingdom, the foreign rule over ישראל
Sprigs or small branches; read here as a hint to the 'lowly' kingdom

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥama bar Ḥanina said:
The son of David will not come
until the lowly kingdom ends from over Israel,
as it is stated: 'And He will cut off the sprigs with pruning hooks,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 18:5. Notice the sound match: זלזלים sounds like זלה, 'lowly.'

phrases.english: and it is written after it:
'At that time a gift will be brought to the Lord of hosts
from a people pulled and plucked.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 18:7. This describes ישראל, scattered and worn down.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר חֲנִינָא: אֵין בֶּן דָּוִד בָּא עַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same 'בן דוד will not come until' pattern to add another sign.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before the משיח comes, the lowly foreign kingdom must stop ruling over ישראל.

steps.title: Arrogant people must disappear from ישראל
steps.stepSummary: זעירי, quoting רבי חנינא, says בן דוד will not come until arrogant people are gone from ישראל. The proof is from צפניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said in the name of רבי חנינא: בן דוד will not come until the arrogant people are gone from ישראל. As it says: 'For then I will remove from among you your proud, boasting ones.' And it says: 'And I will leave among you a poor and humble people, and they will trust in the name of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another sign is given: before the משיח comes, the arrogant people among ישראל must be gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sign is about the inner character of the Jewish people, not outside events. The first פסוק says the proud will be removed, and the next says a humble people will be left who trust in ה׳. Only that humble people is ready for redemption.

phrases.english: Ze'eiri said that Rabbi Ḥanina said:
The son of David will not come
until the arrogant are gone from Israel,
as it is stated: 'For then I will remove from among you
your proud, boasting ones,'
and it is written: 'And I will leave among you a poor and humble people,
and they will trust in the name of the Lord.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר זְעֵירִי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: אֵין בֶּן דָּוִד בָּא עַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another sign in the same pattern, this time about the character of the people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before the משיח comes, the arrogant must be gone from ישראל, leaving a humble people.

steps.title: All judges and officers must disappear from ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמלאי, in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, says בן דוד will not come until all judges and officers are gone from ישראל. He proves it from ישעיהו, where ה׳ promises to restore judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמלאי said in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: בן דוד will not come until all judges and officers are gone from ישראל. As it says: 'And I will turn My hand against you and purge away your impurities as with lye, etc. And I will restore your judges.'
steps.whatsHappening: The last sign in this group: before the משיח comes, all of ישראל's judges and officers will be gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ה׳ will purge away the impurities, then 'restore your judges.' If judges must be restored, the current ones must first be removed. So the disappearance of the present judges comes before the redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: Officers who carry out the judges' rulings
Impurities or dross removed when refining metal

steps.whatToRemember: All four statements here follow one pattern: 'בן דוד will not come until...' something is gone, proved from a פסוק that describes that removal followed by redemption.
steps.confusionAlert: Losing the judges is not described as a good thing in itself. It is a step that comes before ה׳ restores proper judges.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Simlai said in the name of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon:
The son of David will not come

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיִּכְלוּ כׇּל שׁוֹפְטִים וְשׁוֹטְרִים מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: until all judges and officers are gone from Israel,
as it is stated: 'And I will turn My hand against you
and purge away your impurities as with lye, etc.
And I will restore your judges.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: אֵין בֶּן דָּוִד בָּא עַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of signs with one more condition, using the same pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before the משיח comes, all judges and officers will be gone from ישראל; afterward ה׳ will restore proper judges.

steps.title: ירושלים is redeemed only through צדקה
steps.stepSummary: עולא teaches that ירושלים will be redeemed only through צדקה, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: ירושלים will be redeemed only through righteousness, as the פסוק says: 'ציון shall be redeemed with justice, and those who return to it with righteousness.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא adds a new teaching about the גאולה: it depends on צדקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps listed signs that come before the משיח. עולא moves from signs to a cause: righteousness is what brings the redemption. He reads the second half of the פסוק, 'with righteousness,' as the key condition.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Jerusalem is redeemed only through righteousness,
as it says: "Zion shall be redeemed with justice,"
"and those who return to it with righteousness."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: אֵין יְרוּשָׁלָיִם נִפְדֵּית אֶלָּא בִּצְדָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of teachings about the גאולה, adding a condition instead of a sign.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The redemption of ירושלים comes only through צדקה.

steps.title: When arrogance and corrupt judges end, the oppressors end too
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא teaches that once the arrogant are gone from ישראל, the foreign sorcerers will be gone, and once the crooked judges are gone, the oppressive officers will be gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If the arrogant disappear, the sorcerers disappear. If the judges disappear, the royal officers disappear.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא builds on the two earlier teachings about arrogant people and judges, and connects them to the foreign powers that rule over ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 12 and 13 said בן דוד comes when the arrogant and the judges are gone. רב פפא adds a 'measure for measure' link: ישראל's own faults keep their outside oppressors in place. Fix the inside, and the outside pressure goes away.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
If the arrogant cease, the sorcerers cease;
if the judges cease, the royal officers cease.
phrases.notes: He is picking up the judges from רבי שמלאי's teaching just before this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אִי בָּטְלִי יְהִירֵי – בָּטְלִי אַמְגּוּשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on steps 12 and 13 by linking ישראל's inner faults to the foreign oppressors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When arrogance and corrupt judges end among ישראל, the foreign sorcerers and officers end as well.

steps.title: רב פפא's verses for both parts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats each half of רב פפא's teaching and gives a פסוק for each: one from ישעיהו and one from צפניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the arrogant cease, the sorcerers cease, as it is written: 'I will purge away your dross as with lye, and I will remove all your alloy.' And if the judges cease, the officers cease, as it is written: 'ה׳ has removed your judgments; He has cleared away your enemy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רב פפא's two lines, this time to prove each one from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first פסוק, removing the 'dross' (the arrogant) goes together with removing the 'alloy' (the sorcerers). In the second, removing 'your judgments' (the corrupt judges) is paired right away with clearing out 'your enemy' (the oppressive officers). Each פסוק puts the two removals side by side.

keyTerms.meaning: your dross, the waste melted out of metal

phrases.english: If the arrogant cease, the sorcerers cease,
as it is written: "And I will purge away your dross as with lye,"
"and I will remove all your alloy."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:25. The dross stands for the arrogant, and the alloy for the sorcerers, who are separated from fearing ה׳.

phrases.english: And if the judges cease, the royal officers cease,
as it is written: "The Lord has removed your judgments;"
"He has cleared away your enemy."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּטְלִי יְהִירֵי בָּטְלִי אַמְגּוּשֵׁי, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural source for each half of רב פפא's statement in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that ending inner arrogance and corruption ends the outer oppressors.

steps.title: A shrinking generation: wait for the משיח
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that if you see a generation getting smaller and weaker, you should wait for the משיח, based on a פסוק about ה׳ saving a poor people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: If you see a generation that keeps shrinking, wait for him, as it says: 'And the poor people You will save, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a hopeful sign: a generation in decline is a reason to expect the משיח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually decline sounds like bad news. רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק to say that ה׳ saves the 'poor' people, so a weak, shrinking generation is just the kind that will be redeemed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
If you see a generation that keeps getting smaller,
phrases.notes: He means shrinking in Torah and wisdom.

phrases.english: wait for him,
as it says: "And the poor people You will save, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אִם רָאִיתָ דּוֹר שֶׁמִּתְמַעֵט וְהוֹלֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another sign of the coming גאולה, from a new speaker.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A generation in decline should expect the משיח.

steps.title: A generation flooded with troubles: wait for the משיח
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that if troubles pour onto a generation like a river, wait for the משיח, because the פסוק about troubles like a river sits right next to 'a redeemer will come to Zion.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: If you see a generation that many troubles come upon like a river, wait for him, as it says: 'When distress comes like a river, the spirit of ה׳ drives it,' and right next to it: 'And a redeemer will come to ציון.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second sign: heavy, flooding troubles mean the משיח is close.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof uses two פסוקים placed one after the other. Because the river of trouble is followed right away by the redeemer, he learns that the troubles lead into the גאולה.

keyTerms.meaning: right next to it (the very next פסוק)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
If you see a generation that many troubles
come upon like a river,
wait for him,
as it says: "When distress comes like a river,"
"the spirit of the Lord drives it,"
and right next to it: "And a redeemer will come to Zion."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אִם רָאִיתָ דּוֹר שֶׁצָּרוֹת רַבּוֹת בָּאוֹת עָלָיו כַּנָּהָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching by the same speaker, using the same 'if you see, wait for him' pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A generation overwhelmed by troubles should expect the משיח.

steps.title: משיח comes to a generation that is all innocent or all guilty
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that בן דוד comes only to a generation that is completely righteous or completely guilty, and proves each half from ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: בן דוד comes only in a generation that is entirely innocent or entirely guilty. Entirely innocent, as it is written: 'And your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.' Entirely guilty, as it is written: 'And He saw that there was no man, and was astonished that there was no one to pray,' and it is written: 'For My own sake I will do it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן says the משיח comes at one of two extremes: when everyone deserves it, or when no one does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fully righteous generation earns the גאולה, as the first פסוק shows. A fully guilty generation has no one to pray for it, so ה׳ redeems them 'for My own sake' and not because of their merit. A mixed generation fits neither path.

keyTerms.meaning: one who prays and pleads on others' behalf

steps.confusionAlert: The guilty generation is not redeemed because it deserves it. The second פסוק shows ה׳ acts 'for My own sake,' since no one is there to plead for them.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The son of David comes only

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּדוֹר שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ זַכַּאי, אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: in a generation that is entirely innocent, or entirely guilty.
In a generation that is entirely innocent, as it is written:
"And your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever."
In a generation that is entirely guilty, as it is written:
"And He saw that there was no man,"
"and was astonished that there was no one to plead,"
and it is written: "For My own sake I will do it."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין בֶּן דָּוִד בָּא אֶלָּא בְּדוֹר שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ זַכַּאי, אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third teaching from רבי יוחנן, now about the moral state of the generation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן דוד comes only to a fully righteous generation, which earns it, or a fully guilty one, which ה׳ redeems for His own sake.

steps.title: One verse says 'in its time' and also 'I will hasten it'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי points out a contradiction within a פסוק: it says the גאולה comes 'in its time' and also that ה׳ will 'hasten it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלכסנדרי said: רבי יהושע בן לוי raised a contradiction: it is written 'in its time,' and it is written 'I will hasten it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a puzzle: a set time and hurrying seem to clash. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In its time' means there is a fixed date for the גאולה. 'I will hasten it' means it can come early. Both cannot be simply true at once, so the words need to be explained.

phrases.english: Rabbi Alexandri said:
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi raised a contradiction:
It is written "in its time,"
and it is written "I will hasten it."
phrases.notes: Both words are in the same פסוק, ישעיהו 60:22.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי רָמֵי, כְּתִיב ״בְּעִתָּהּ״ וּכְתִיב ״אֲחִישֶׁנָּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: whether the time of the גאולה is fixed or can be moved earlier.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A fixed time ('in its time') seems to rule out bringing it early ('I will hasten it').

steps.title: If they merit, it is hastened; if not, it comes in its time
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction is resolved: if ישראל are worthy, ה׳ brings the גאולה early, and if not, it comes at its set time.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they merit, 'I will hasten it'; if they do not merit, 'in its time.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying each phrase fits a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a fixed latest date, 'in its time.' But ישראל's merit can bring it sooner, 'I will hasten it.' So the two phrases do not clash; they describe two possible outcomes.
steps.whatToRemember: The גאולה has a set latest time, but merit can bring it earlier. So both a fixed time and ישראל's merit play a part, which echoes both sides of the earlier debate between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: If they merit — "I will hasten it";
if they do not merit — "in its time."

steps.triggerLanguage: זָכוּ – אֲחִישֶׁנָּה, לֹא זָכוּ – בְּעִתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two phrases into two different situations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to say both that the time is fixed and that it can be moved earlier.
steps.terutzMaskana: Merit brings the גאולה early; without merit it comes at its set time.

steps.title: Clouds of heaven or a poor man on a donkey?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלכסנדרי reports that רבי יהושע בן לוי pointed out a contradiction between two פסוקים describing how משיח will arrive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלכסנדרי said: רבי יהושע בן לוי pointed out a contradiction. One פסוק says משיח comes with the clouds of heaven. Another says he comes poor and riding on a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two פסוקים that seem to describe משיח's arrival in opposite ways: one grand and one humble.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דניאל, משיח arrives in glory on the clouds of heaven. In זכריה, he arrives poor and riding on a simple donkey. Both cannot describe the same arrival, so we need an explanation. This follows the same pattern as the 'in its time' and 'I will hasten it' question in Step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises a contradiction (sets two sources against each other)
Like a son of man (a human figure)
Poor and riding on a donkey

phrases.english: Rabbi Alexandri says:
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi raises a contradiction:
It is written: "And behold, with the clouds of heaven
one like a son of man came,"
and it is written: "Poor and riding on a donkey."

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יהושע בן לוי רמי כתיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second contradiction from רבי יהושע בן לוי about the גאולה, built the same way as Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים describing how משיח will arrive
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק describes a glorious arrival on the clouds and the other a humble arrival on a donkey. These cannot both describe the same event.

steps.title: It depends on whether ישראל are worthy
steps.stepSummary: If ישראל are worthy, משיח comes on the clouds. If not, he comes poor on a donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they are worthy, he comes with the clouds of heaven. If they are not worthy, he comes poor and riding on a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each פסוק describes a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים are true, but they describe two possible futures. If ישראל are worthy, the גאולה comes in a glorious, miraculous way. If they are not, it comes in a humble way. This matches Step 21, where being worthy decides whether the גאולה comes early.
steps.whatToRemember: How משיח arrives, gloriously or humbly, depends on how worthy ישראל are, just as the timing does.

phrases.english: If they are worthy: with the clouds of heaven.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא זָכוּ – עָנִי וְרוֹכֵב עַל חֲמוֹר.
phrases.english: If they are not worthy: poor and riding on a donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: זכו עם ענני שמיא לא זכו עני ורוכב על חמור
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each פסוק applies to a different situation (worthy or not worthy)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to describe one single way משיח will come.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two possible ways, and which one happens depends on whether ישראל are worthy.

steps.title: King שבור mocks the idea of a donkey
steps.stepSummary: The Persian king שבור mocks שמואל: if your משיח comes on a donkey, I will send him my fine horse.
steps.simpleTranslation: King שבור said to שמואל: You say משיח comes on a donkey? I'll send him the fine horse that I have!
steps.whatsHappening: A non-Jewish king makes fun of the idea that משיח will ride a donkey. This sets up שמואל's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבור takes the donkey picture to mean that משיח will be poor and unimpressive. He offers his own fine horse as an insult, as if משיח could not even afford a proper animal.

phrases.english: King Shapur said to Shmuel:
You say the Messiah comes on a donkey?

phrases.aramaic: אֵישַׁדַּר לֵיהּ סוּסְיָא בָּרְקָא דְּאִית לִי!
phrases.english: I will send him the fine riding horse that I have!

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה שבור מלכא לשמואל אמריתו משיח על חמרא אתי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the 'poor and riding on a donkey' image in Steps 22 and 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that משיח will come riding on a donkey
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Arriving on a donkey sounds lowly, so שבור mocks it by offering a better animal.

steps.title: שמואל: Do you have a horse of many colors?
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that משיח's donkey is special, with many colors, and no horse of שבור could match it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you have one of a thousand colors?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל turns the insult around by saying משיח's donkey is no ordinary animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבור assumed the donkey shows weakness. שמואל answers that משיח's donkey is miraculous and has many colors. Even the 'humble' arrival is greater than any king's finest horse.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מִי אִית לָךְ בַּר חֵיוַר גַּוְונֵי?
phrases.english: Do you have one of a thousand colors?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה מי אית לך בר חיור גווני
steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל answers שבור's mockery from Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes the image: the donkey is miraculous, not lowly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A donkey means משיח is poor and unimpressive.
steps.terutzMaskana: משיח's donkey is wondrous and far beyond any king's horse.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי meets אליהו and asks about עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי finds אליהו at the cave of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי and asks whether he will reach עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי found אליהו standing at the entrance of the cave of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי. He asked him: Will I come to עולם הבא?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins: רבי יהושע בן לוי meets אליהו and asks him a personal question. אליהו answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story opens a new section that will lead to questions about משיח. First, רבי יהושע בן לוי asks about his own share in עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: עולם הבא, the World to Come

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אַשְׁכַּח לְאֵלִיָּהוּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi found Elijah
who was standing at the entrance
of the cave of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai.
He said to him: Will I come to the World to Come?

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יהושע בן לוי אשכח לאליהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about the coming of משיח.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהושע בן לוי will merit עולם הבא

steps.title: 'If this Master wants': a third presence
steps.stepSummary: אליהו answers 'if this Master wants it,' and רבי יהושע בן לוי says he saw two but heard the voice of three.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If this Master wants. רבי יהושע בן לוי said: I saw two, but I heard the voice of three.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו answers that it depends on 'this Master.' רבי יהושע בן לוי then explains that someone else was there with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only רבי יהושע בן לוי and אליהו could be seen, yet אליהו spoke of 'this Master' as if He were present. רבי יהושע בן לוי understood that the שכינה was there, so he 'heard three' although he saw only two.

keyTerms.meaning: If this Master wants (referring to ה׳)
Two I saw, and the voice of three I heard

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם יִרְצֶה אָדוֹן הַזֶּה.
phrases.english: He said to him: If this Master wants.
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Two I saw, and the voice of three I heard.
phrases.notes: He saw only himself and אליהו, but the 'Master' who was spoken of, the שכינה, was there too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה אם ירצה אדון הזה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives אליהו's answer to the question in Step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It depends on the will of ה׳, who was present there.

steps.title: When will משיח come?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי asks אליהו when משיח will come.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When will משיח come?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי asks the big question of the whole sugya: when will משיח arrive? אליהו's answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This brings the story back to the main topic of the surrounding steps, the timing of the גאולה.

phrases.english: He said to him: When will the Messiah come?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה אימת אתי משיח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After asking about himself, he now asks about משיח.

steps.title: Go ask משיח himself, at the gate of רומי
steps.stepSummary: אליהו tells him to ask משיח directly, and says משיח sits at the entrance of רומי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go ask him yourself. And where does he sit? At the entrance of רומי.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of giving a date, אליהו sends רבי יהושע בן לוי to ask משיח himself and tells him where to find him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהו does not answer the 'when' question directly. Surprisingly, משיח is already present in the world, sitting at the gate of רומי, and can be approached.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go ask him himself.
And where is he sitting?
At the entrance of Rome.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה זיל שייליה לדידיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אליהו responds to the question of Step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Ask משיח directly; he sits at the entrance of רומי.

steps.title: How to recognize משיח: one bandage at a time
steps.stepSummary: משיח sits among sick poor people. They all change their bandages at once, but he does one at a time so he can be ready immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is his sign? He sits among poor people who suffer from illnesses. All of them untie and tie their bandages at one time, but he unties one and ties one. He says: Perhaps I will be needed, so I should not be delayed.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו gives the sign for recognizing משיח: he is always ready to leave at a moment's notice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other sick people undo all their bandages and rebind them together. משיח undoes only one bandage at a time, so that if he is called to bring the גאולה, he will not lose time rebinding them all. He is always prepared.

keyTerms.meaning: So that I will not be delayed

steps.whatToRemember: משיח is pictured as already waiting and always ready, taking care never to be delayed even by a moment.

phrases.english: And what is his sign?
He sits among poor people who suffer from illnesses,
and all of them untie and tie at one time,
phrases.notes: They are undoing and rebinding their bandages.

phrases.english: but he unties one and ties one.
He says: Perhaps I will be needed, so that I will not be delayed.

steps.triggerLanguage: ומאי סימניה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אליהו's directions with the sign for recognizing משיח.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משיח changes one bandage at a time so he is always ready to come right away.

steps.title: Greeting משיח and asking when he will come
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי goes to משיח. They greet each other, and he asks משיח when he will come.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went to him and said: Peace upon you, my rabbi and my teacher! משיח answered: Peace upon you, son of Levi. He asked: When will the Master come?
steps.whatsHappening: Following אליהו's advice, רבי יהושע בן לוי finds משיח, greets him, and asks the big question directly. This sets up משיח's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי speaks with great respect and calls משיח 'my rabbi and my teacher.' משיח answers his greeting and calls him by his father's name. The details of this greeting will matter later, when אליהו explains what it meant.

phrases.english: He went to him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is משיח, sitting at the entrance of רומי, as described in step 29.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שָׁלוֹם עָלֶיךָ רַבִּי וּמוֹרִי!
phrases.english: He said to him: Peace upon you, my rabbi and my teacher!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שָׁלוֹם עָלֶיךָ בַּר לֵיוַאי.
phrases.english: He said to him: Peace upon you, son of Levi.
He said to him: When will the Master come?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְאֵימַת אָתֵי מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out אליהו's instruction from step 29 to go ask משיח directly.

steps.title: משיח answers: Today
steps.stepSummary: משיח answers that he will come today.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Today.
steps.whatsHappening: משיח gives a one-word answer: 'today.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer sounds like a clear promise about the date. That is exactly why it causes a problem a few steps later, when he does not come.

phrases.english: He said to him: Today.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 31.

steps.title: אליהו asks what משיח said
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי returns to אליהו, who asks what משיח told him. He repeats משיח's greeting.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came to אליהו. אליהו asked: What did he say to you? He answered: He said 'Peace upon you, son of Levi.'
steps.whatsHappening: The scene moves back to אליהו, who asks for a report. This sets up אליהו's explanation of the greeting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי reports the greeting first. אליהו will read meaning into it.

keyTerms.meaning: what did he say to you?

phrases.english: He came to Elijah.
He said to him: What did he say to you?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שָׁלוֹם עָלֶיךָ בַּר לֵיוַאי.
phrases.english: He said to him: 'Peace upon you, son of Levi.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי אֲמַר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves back to אליהו for an explanation of the meeting.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What משיח said to רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: The greeting promised עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: אליהו explains that משיח's greeting guaranteed עולם הבא for him and his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He guaranteed you and your father עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו explains that by greeting him with 'peace,' משיח promised עולם הבא to רבי יהושע בן לוי and his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the question from step 26, whether רבי יהושע בן לוי will reach עולם הבא. The words 'son of Levi' in the greeting explain why his father is included too.

phrases.english: He said to him: He guaranteed you and your father
the World-to-Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַבְטְחָךְ לָךְ וְלַאֲבוּךְ לְעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interprets the greeting reported in step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'peace' greeting promised עולם הבא to him and his father.

steps.title: Complaint: משיח said today and did not come
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי complains that משיח lied, because he said he would come today and did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He lied to me, because he told me 'I am coming today,' and he did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי raises a challenge. 'Today' has passed and משיח has not come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we read 'today' simply, משיח's answer turned out false. That forces us to find a different way to understand his words.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שַׁקּוֹרֵי קָא שַׁקַּר בִּי,
phrases.english: He said to him: He lied to me,
for he said to me, 'I am coming today,'
and he did not come.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁקּוֹרֵי קָא שַׁקַּר בִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'today' answer from step 32.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The day passed without משיח coming, so the answer seems false.

steps.title: Today, if you listen to His voice
steps.stepSummary: אליהו explains that משיח was quoting a פסוק: 'today, if you will listen to His voice.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what he told you: 'Today, if you will listen to His voice.'
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו answers the complaint. משיח's 'today' was a quote from a פסוק, and the פסוק includes a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Today' was never a fixed date. It is a promise that depends on us: משיח can come any day that the people listen to ה׳'s voice. This links back to step 30, where משיח is shown always ready to come at once.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what he told you
if you will listen to His voice

steps.whatToRemember: משיח's 'today' is conditional. He is ready to come any day, as soon as the people listen to ה׳'s voice.
steps.confusionAlert: משיח did not lie. 'Today' was the start of a פסוק that has a condition built into it.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what he told you:
'Today, if you will listen to His voice.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר לָךְ: הַיּוֹם אִם בְּקֹלוֹ תִשְׁמָעוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 35.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the words as a quote from a פסוק that contains a condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Today' meant a fixed date, so משיח lied.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Today' depends on the people listening to ה׳'s voice.

steps.title: Students ask רבי יוסי בן קיסמא when בן דוד will come
steps.stepSummary: The students ask when בן דוד will come. He worries they will want a sign, and they promise they will not ask for one.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students asked רבי יוסי בן קיסמא: When will בן דוד come? He said: I am afraid you will ask me for a sign. They said: We are not asking you for a sign.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins with the same question: when will משיח come? Before answering, the teacher makes his students promise not to demand proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בן קיסמא hesitates because he is afraid they will ask him for a sign to back up his answer. The students' promise sets up the twist later, when they break it.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן קִיסְמָא:
phrases.english: His students asked Rabbi Yosei ben Kisma:
When will the son of David come?
He said: I am afraid
that perhaps you will ask me for a sign.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין אָנוּ מְבַקְּשִׁין מִמְּךָ אוֹת.
phrases.english: They said to him: We are not asking you for a sign.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן קִיסְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story on the same theme: when משיח will come.

steps.title: The gate that falls three times
steps.stepSummary: He answers that a certain gate will fall and be rebuilt twice. After it falls the third time, it will not be rebuilt before בן דוד comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: When this gate falls and is rebuilt, falls and is rebuilt, and falls again, they will not manage to rebuild it before בן דוד comes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בן קיסמא gives his answer as a sequence of events the students can watch for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not give a date. He gives a pattern: two rebuildings, then a third fall with no time left to rebuild before משיח arrives.

phrases.english: He said to them: When this gate falls,
and is rebuilt, and falls and is rebuilt, and falls,
and they will not manage to rebuild it
before the son of David comes.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִכְשֶׁיִּפּוֹל הַשַּׁעַר הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question from step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After the gate falls a third time, משיח will come before it can be rebuilt.

steps.title: The students ask for a sign after all
steps.stepSummary: The students ask for a sign anyway. He reminds them that they promised not to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Our rabbi, give us a sign! He said: Didn't you tell me you would not ask me for a sign?
steps.whatsHappening: Exactly as their teacher feared, the students ask for proof. He reminds them of their promise, which sets up their reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fear he voiced in step 37 comes true. His reply holds them to their word before he gives in.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: רַבֵּינוּ, תֵּן לָנוּ אוֹת!
phrases.english: They said to him: Our rabbi, give us a sign!

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: וְלֹא כָּךְ אֲמַרְתֶּם לִי
phrases.english: He said to them: But did you not say this to me,
that you are not asking me for a sign?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבֵּינוּ, תֵּן לָנוּ אוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The students break the promise they made in step 37.

steps.title: The waters of פמייס turn to blood
steps.stepSummary: The students insist. He says that if his words are true, the waters of the cave of פמייס will turn to blood, and they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Even so. He said to them: If so, may the waters of the cave of פמייס turn to blood. And they turned to blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The teacher gives in and names a sign, and it comes true: the water turns to blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The miracle confirms that his prediction about the gate is true. The story of רבי יוסי בן קיסמא is not over yet: the next step moves on to his instructions at the time of his death.

keyTerms.meaning: the cave of פמייס, a spring

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי בן קיסמא's prediction about the gate was confirmed by a miracle: the waters of פמייס turned to blood.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן.
phrases.english: They said to him: And even so.
phrases.notes: They mean: we know we promised, but please give us a sign anyway.

phrases.english: He said to them: If it is so,
may the waters of the cave of Pamyas turn to blood.
And they turned to blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵהָפְכוּ מֵי מְעָרַת פַּמְיָיס לְדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the sign the students asked for in step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A miraculous sign: the waters of פמייס turned to blood, confirming the prediction.

steps.title: On his deathbed, he asks for his coffin to be buried deep
steps.stepSummary: As רבי יוסי בן קיסמא is dying, he tells his students to bury his coffin deep in the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the time of his death, he said to them: Bury my coffin deep in the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward to the moment of רבי יוסי בן קיסמא's death, and he gives his students a burial instruction. This line is a setup: the גמרא explains why he wants his coffin buried deep on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the students asked questions and he answered them about when בן דוד will come. Now he gives them an instruction of his own: dig my grave deeper than usual. The instruction is surprising, which makes the reader wait for the explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of his passing, meaning when he was dying
Make deep, meaning dig deep or place deep

phrases.english: At the time of his death, he said to them:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יוסי בן קיסמא, and "them" means his students from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: Place my coffin deep in the ground,

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁעַת פְּטִירָתוֹ, אָמַר לָהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רבי יוסי בן קיסמא and his students after the sign of the waters of פמייס, moving to his final instructions at his death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי בן קיסמא instructs his students to bury his coffin deep in the ground. The reason is given on the next amud.
